grammar.label: register shift inside a sentence
grammar.form: a formal frame with a colloquial word, or the reverse
grammar.meaning: produces irony, warmth or contempt by mixing levels

explanation.en: 'The Board has determined that the scheme is, in a word, rubbish.' The shock of the last word is the whole effect, and it works only because everything before it was formal. Done once, it lands; done three times, the formal frame stops being a frame.
explanation.uz: 'The Board has determined that the scheme is, in a word, rubbish.' Oxirgi so'zning zarbasi — butun ta'sir, va u faqat oldingi hamma narsa rasmiy bo'lgani uchun ishlaydi.

grammar.positive_example: The committee considered the proposal at length and then, frankly, lost its nerve.
grammar.negative_example: The committee, like, considered the proposal and then, frankly, lost its nerve.

l1_notes.uz: Uslublar aralashuvi ingliz tilida kuchli vosita; o'zbek yozma an'anasida u ko'proq xato sifatida qabul qilinadi.

grammar.label: euphemism, dysphemism and the honest word
grammar.form: collateral damage / civilian deaths; let go / dismissed; passed away / died
grammar.meaning: chooses how much of a thing the reader is made to feel

explanation.en: Every euphemism is an argument about how much reality the reader should be handed. 'Passed away' is kindness at a funeral and evasion in a coroner's report. The C2 skill is not to avoid euphemism — that is its own affectation — but to know what each choice does to the reader and to choose deliberately.
explanation.uz: Har bir yumshatma — o'quvchiga qancha haqiqat berilishi haqidagi bahs. 'Passed away' dafn marosimida mehribonlik, ammo tibbiy hisobotda qochish.

grammar.positive_example: The report says 'let go'; the tribunal papers say 'dismissed'; both describe the same afternoon.
grammar.negative_example: The report says 'let go', which is the polite and therefore the correct word.

l1_notes.uz: Yumshatma so'zlar madaniyatga bog'liq; ingliz rasmiy tilida ular juda ko'p va ko'pincha sezilmaydi.

body.text: 'The committee has considered the proposal at length and finds it, in a word, useless.'

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: The last three words are not the same English as the first ten.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: They are not, and that is why they land. A shift inside one sentence is a hammer. Use it once in a report.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I had written 'the committee is of the view that certain difficulties may arise'.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Which says nothing at all. Who is going to act on 'certain difficulties may arise'?

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: That is a euphemism doing the work it should do and the work it should not, in the same breath. It softens the blow and it hides the fact.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Often. You write 'she died' to a colleague and 'we lost her' to her sister, and both are honest.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: And 'we are moving to a smaller team'?

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Eleven people lost their jobs. That is the sentence somebody went to a great deal of trouble to avoid.
